{{Quote|You're among the best pilots in the galaxy. You'll have to be if you want to control this starship.|[[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Gial Ackbar/Legends|Ackbar]] briefing B-wing [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] prior to the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]]|<ref name="NEGVV" />}}
The '''A/SF-01 B-wing heavy assault starfighter''', known simply as the '''B-wing starfighter''', was one of the largest and most heavily armed [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]]/[[Bomber/Legends|bombers]] in the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance's]] [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|fleet]]. The name B-wing came from the craft's appearance to a [[High Galactic/Legends|High Galactic]] "B", when upright, the outline of the upper half and the lower half making a B shape, although its swordlike shape in attack mode earned it the nickname "Blade-wing", which may have been another reason for the "B" prefix.

Known as "crosses" due to their distinct shape, the B-wing was designed by the [[Verpine/Legends|Verpine]] company [[Slayn & Korpil/Legends|Slayn & Korpil]] in cooperation with then-[[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Gial Ackbar/Legends|Gial Ackbar]] as part of the [[Shantipole Project]]. The B-wing, though difficult to fly, participated in numerous engagements across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] during the latter parts of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], including the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] and the [[Liberation of Coruscant (Galactic Civil War)|liberation of Coruscant]]. The B-wing was used in its primary role of assault starfighter by both the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] and the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]] throughout the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]] and beyond.

Later models included a [[B-wing/E starfighter|two-man version]] that could be used as a small [[Transport/Legends|transport]].

==Characteristics==
{{Quote|Because the cockpit is surrounded by a unique gyro-stabilization system, the pilot always remains stationary, even as the rest of the ship rotates during flight.|[[General/Legends|General]] [[Carlist Rieekan/Legends|Carlist Rieekan]]|<ref name="RS II">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Bwing_egvv.jpg|thumb|left|150px|B-wing [[:Category:Technical drawing images|schematics]]]]
The A/SF-01 B-wing assault [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] had a somewhat ungainly appearance resembling a top-heavy cross when fully unfurled. The primary airfoil took up the length of the hull, with the [[Cockpit/Legends|cockpit]] at one end and a weapons pod at the other end. Two [[S-foils/Legends|S-foils]] amidships on either side of the airfoil also held weapons.<ref name="SWE">''[[StarWars.com]] [[Encyclopedia (StarWars.com)|Encyclopedia]]'' entry</ref> In addition, the B-wing's main body was essentially a single long wing with a pair of folding S-foils. Its primary role was an attack vessel targeting the Empire's capital ships, although it also did escort duty for X- and Y-wing fighter squadrons and Alliance convoys, and were also able to be deployed for assaults on space-based or planetary Imperial facilities.<ref name="CCS" />

The B-wing was a highly adaptable design, with modular hardpoints and other components. Its weapons could be reconfigured more easily than many other Alliance fighters. The B-wing also had a unique gyroscopic rotating cockpit module which was independently stabilized to allow the pilot to coordinate advanced flight and attack maneuvers. The fighter was powered by either of two engine systems: a [[Quadex/Legends|Quadex]] [[Kyromaster ion engine/Legends|Kyromaster]] engine with four thrust ports, or four Slayn & Korpil [[JZ-5 Fusial Thrust Engine]]s.<ref name="SC" /> The Quadex core was the same version carried on-board [[Corellian Engineering Corporation/Legends|CEC]] [[YT-1300 light freighter/Legends|YT-1300 light freighters]]. The rotating airfoil allowed the B-wing to be placed vertical in launch racks,<ref name="EGW" /> although it was also capable of landing horizontally.<ref name="RS II" />

[[File:Bwing-sag.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Rear view of a B-wing]]
[[Vinop O2 K cryogenic power cell]]s and an [[ionization reactor]] fueled the ship,<ref name="SC" /> and Slayn & Korpil [[HYd-997 hyperdrive motivator/Legends|HYd-997 hyperdrive motivator]] was a Class 2 [[Hyperdrive/Legends|lightspeed]] system.<ref name="BtM" /> A [[Sirplex/Legends|Sirplex]] [[Zr-41 shield generator/Legends|Zr-41 shield generator]],<ref name="SC" /> rated at 100 [[SBD/Legends|SBD]],<ref name="XWA" /> and a reinforced [[Durasteel/Legends|durasteel]] rated at 60 [[RU/Legends|RU]]<ref name="XWA" /> provided protection.

The B-wing carried a [[Fabritech/Legends|Fabritech]] [[ANv-9q Sensor Array]] with [[PH-5s Phased Tachyon Detection Array]] and [[PK-8f Primary Threat Analysis Grid]], and its targeting computer was an [[ANq 3.6 sensor computer/Legends|ANq 3.6 system]] with [[IN-344-B "Sightline" holographic imaging system/Legends|IN-344-B "Sightline" holographic imaging system]]. The [[Navigation computer/Legends|navigation computer]] was a [[Microaxial/Legends|Microaxial]] [[LpM-549 Navigation Sensor|LpM-549 unit]], and the starfighter was equipped with a [[Narmox]] [[HG.6w flight control avionics]] system.<ref name="SC" /> The powerful systems were originally designed for small [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ships]].<ref name="EGW" /> The targeting computer was also advanced and connected its armaments to the computer for the purpose of coordinated precision strikes, with assistance from low-power targeting lasers, although it alternated between this and being independently controlled by the pilot.<ref name="CCS" />

The B-wing was also expensive to manufacture.<ref name="EGW" />

[[File:Bwing-cpmodule.jpg|thumb|left|150px|The cockpit module of a B-wing showing the groove allowing for rotation]]
In particular, the rotating hull system made the B-wing a challenge to master. It also made the ship abnormally delicate; too many sharp turns could cause extreme strain to the spaceframe, and the cockpit rotation system could get stuck in one position. Only a few pilots were qualified to fly the ship before the Battle of Endor, resulting in a smaller number of B-wings present than expected. These difficulties forced the Rebel Alliance to invest in an upgraded Y-wing, rather than an entirely new ship, to fulfill their needs. In addition, the gyro-mechanisms for the fighter were prone to in-flight failure, causing the fighters to end up "frozen" into position, thus leading to maneuvering problems. Another problem is that their parked position had all three of its "wings" being locked into position as well as sitting on the lower wing, making access to the central area awkward, and thus maintenance servicing of the overall craft difficult.<ref name="CCS" />

Its weapons systems included three wing-tip ion-cannons, a heavy laser cannon with a low-power targeting laser, twin auto blasters with a low-power targeting laser, a mount for additional weapons consisting of an additional auto-blaster, laser or ion cannon, and two proton torpedo launcher magazines, one that carried four torpedoes on the lower wing launcher and a secondary torpedo launcher magazine just below the cockpit area.<ref name="CCS" />

Like its predecessor, the Y-wing, the cockpit could be detached from the rest of the ship, but unlike the Y-wing, the B-wing's cockpit could be ejected into space and support atmospheric re-entry.<ref name="Star Wars: Rebel Assault II: The Hidden Empire">''[[Star Wars: Rebel Assault II: The Hidden Empire]]''</ref>

The B-wing would go on to participate in many battles throughout the Galactic Civil War, and would lend design elements to other vessels. Sometime after the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]], the hull of a wrecked B-wing was used as the design prototype for the [[AHS-1 heavy assault airspeeder]], and later models followed the same general design. In addition, several B-wings after the Battle of Endor were also modified to include flame-retardant projectors by Alliance technicians so the craft could be used for fire-fighting purposes.<ref name="CCS" />

A typical tactic for B-wing squadrons on attack missions was to utilize dense formations as a means of increasing concentrated firepower on targets. This tactic also has the added benefit of overwhelming most deflector shields.

==Variants==
===B-wing/E "Expanded" starfighter===
{{Main|B-wing/E starfighter}}
The '''B-wing/E starfighter''', or '''B-wing Expanded''', was a modification to the original Slayn & Korpil B-wing design. The B-wing Expanded had an elongated cockpit that allowed a [[Gunner/Legends|gunner]] to assist the pilot on missions. This allowed the pilot to concentrate on piloting, and resulted in the B-wing accounting for an increased number of kills in battle. It was faster and tougher than the original B-wing, but was somewhat less maneuverable. There were two models of B-wing/E, with the second having enhanced torpedo systems.<ref name="TEGtVaV" /> Ackbar used a modified one of these E2-designs as his own shuttle, which he was forced to crash on the planet [[Vortex/Legends|Vortex]] after it had been tampered with by [[Terpfen]].<ref name="Dark">[[Dark Apprentice (novel)|''Dark Apprentice'']]</ref>

===B-wing shuttle===
The '''B-wing shuttle''' was another variant of Slayn & Korpil's B-Wing fighter which was given a larger cockpit allowing it to house a pilot along with two passengers. It was only armed with laser and light ion cannons.<ref name="Starships" />

==Armaments==
[[File:Bwing-NEGVV.png|thumb|right|180px|A B-wing in attack configuration]]
{{Quote|One of the Rebellion's most well-armed starfighters, the B-wing has been personally designed by Admiral Ackbar. The B-wing supports an array of weapons including ion cannons, proton torpedo launchers, and laser cannons.|General Carlist Rieekan|<ref name="RS II" />}}
The B-wing carried one of the most powerful armaments of any Rebellion craft. Its standard configuration included three [[ArMek/Legends|ArMek]] [[SW-7a ion cannon/Legends|SW-7a ion cannons]] mounted on the wing-tips, two [[Krupx Munitions/Legends|Krupx]] [[MG9 proton torpedo launcher/Legends|MG9 proton torpedo launchers]] with four<ref name="CCS" /><ref name="HtH" /> heavy [[Proton torpedo/Legends|proton torpedoes]]<ref name="SotG" /> or six standard torpedoes each,<ref name="Starships" /> mounted on the end of the main wing and above the engines, one [[Gyrhil/Legends|Gyrhil]] [[R-9X heavy laser cannon/Legends|R-9X heavy laser cannon]] on the main wing and two [[Gyrhil/Legends|Gyrhil]] [[72 twin auto-blaster/Legends|72]] [[autoblaster]]s at the cockpit.<ref name="CCS" /> It was possible to include two more autoblasters there. An alternate configuration places all three SW-7a ion cannons to this cockpit hardpoints and a R-9X laser cannon on each wing-tip,<ref name="TEGtVaV" /> with the torpedo launchers holding six torpedoes each.<ref name="SC" /><ref name="XWA" /> Another configuration carried a heavy [[Ion cannon/Legends|ion cannon]], proton torpedoes, auto-blasters and a trio of laser cannons.<ref name="DB">{{DB|starship|bwingstarfighter|B-wing starfighter}}</ref> The launcher was also capable of firing [[Advanced Proton Torpedo/Legends|advanced proton torpedoes]].<ref name="RS II" /> [[Proton bomb/Legends|Proton bombs]]<ref name="AOR Core" /> or [[Mag-pulse warhead/Legends|mag-pulse warheads]] could be launched, too.<ref name="TF">[[Star Wars: TIE Fighter (video game)|''Star Wars: TIE Fighter'']]</ref> The starfighter could also carry additional ordnance on hardpoints under the S-foils.<ref name="Star Wars: Rebellion 14: Small Victories, Part 4" />

While its strong [[Deflector shield/Legends|deflector shields]] and great firepower allowed it to be somewhat survivable in fighter engagements, it usually required an escort on the way in. However, with the firepower of many naval [[Corvette/Legends|corvettes]], it fulfilled its purpose as a dangerous foe against many light capital ships.

==History==
[[File:Rebel_Aces_Expansion_Pack_box_art.png|thumb|left|220px|A B-wing and an A-wing being pursued by Imperial TIE fighters]]
The development of the B-wing began shortly after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. The small-unit starfighter tactics of the Rebellion were having a greater effect on the forces of the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] than many [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] commanders thought possible. As a response to this threat, the Empire began to produce and deploy more [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ships]] with a primary role of anti-starfighter defense. The primary vessel used for this strategy was the [[EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate/Legends|EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate]], a starship with which the Alliance was already quite familiar.

The Rebels couldn't afford to field the kind of overwhelming space forces that the Empire could bring to bear in fleet engagements. The Alliance's primary assault fighters, the outdated Y-wings, took large losses in capital ship assaults. A new tactic was needed if the Rebel Alliance Fleet was to continue having any impact on the galaxy.

Fortunately, one advantage the Rebels had over the Empire was their people. Approximately a [[1 BBY/Legends|year before]] the Battle of Yavin, the Rebels executed a raid on an Imperial [[Lambda-class T-4a shuttle/Legends|''Lambda''-class shuttle]] carrying [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]] and [[Bevel Lemelisk]] near [[Eriadu/Legends|Eriadu]]. The Alliance rescued the renowned [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] tactician Ackbar, in a military operation the Empire might not have bothered to commit for one of their own personnel.<ref name="Darksaber">[[Darksaber (novel)|''Darksaber'']]</ref> As a commander in the Alliance Fleet, Ackbar revolutionized the strategy and tactics of the Alliance.

[[File:BWingFirefighter-RogueLeaderI1P4.jpg|thumb|right|220px|B-wings retrofitted for firefighting duty on [[Endor/Legends|Endor]]]]
Ackbar knew that the only solution to the Empire's new convoy defense plan was to either use equally powerful starships, which the Alliance could not afford to waste, or to create a starfighter especially for this purpose. [[Alliance High Command/Legends|Alliance High Command]] agreed, and placed Ackbar in charge of Project Shantipole. Ackbar went to the Roche system and enlisted the aid of the Verpine colonies of Slayn & Korpil.

Working under Ackbar's direction, Slayn & Korpil produced the first prototypes of the B-wing starfighter in the [[Roche asteroid field]]. They were delivered to the Alliance despite Imperial interference. Imperial District Commander [[Bane Nothos]] was aware of the project, and decided to allow development to proceed so he could capture the fighters for the Empire. The Empire's efforts to capture the blueprints of the B-wing were actually foiled by the first combat flight of the original prototypes.<ref name="Strike Force: Shantipole">''[[Strike Force: Shantipole]]''</ref> A squadron of these prototypes was quickly put into service and christened [[Dagger Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Dagger Squadron]].<ref name="Star Wars: Rebellion 14: Small Victories, Part 4" />

After the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]], [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]] [[Rogue Leader/Legends|Leader]] [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]] flew a B-wing during a [[Prison/Legends|prison]] [[Raid at Bakura|liberation]] on the [[Bakura Imperial Prison]].<ref name="RS III">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]''</ref> He also flew it in an [[Battle of Kothlis|assault]] against the [[Motivator (Imperial-class)|''Motivator'']] above [[Kothlis/Legends|Kothlis]].<ref name="RS II" />

[[File:BWingsKillISD2-ST.jpg|thumb|left|220px|B-wings flee from an exploding [[Imperial II-class Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] during the Battle of Endor.]]

Despite its limited numbers at the time, it was a key Rebel craft in the Battle of [[Endor/Legends|Endor]], where a squad of these fighters took down two [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyers]].<ref name="EGW" /> After the battle, the B-wing's modular design allowed it to be retrofitted with sprayers for firefighting duty on Endor, to extinguish the fires caused by the falling debris.<ref name="X-Wing: Rogue Leader">''[[Star Wars: X-Wing: Rogue Leader]]''</ref>

B-wings were present in the [[Invasion of Bakura]],<ref name="The Truce at Bakura">''[[The Truce at Bakura]]''</ref> and at least one B-wing squadron, [[Lancer Squadron (New Republic)|Lancer Squadron]], was present at the [[Liberation of Coruscant (Galactic Civil War)|liberation]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], where it supported an army group led by [[General/Legends|General]] [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]].<ref name="SW:GB:CC" /> The B-wing fighter also featured significantly in the campaign against Warlord [[Zsinj]]: [[Guardian Squadron]] of General [[Horton Salm/Legends|Horton Salm's]] [[Defender Wing]] was retrofitted with B-wings for a [[raid on Yag-prime]],<ref name="X-Wing: TKT">''[[X-Wing: The Krytos Trap]]''</ref> and the B-wings of [[Nova Squadron/Legends|Nova Squadron]] were instrumental in defeating the [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyers]] ''[[Razor's Kiss]]''<ref name="X-Wing: Iron Fist">''[[X-Wing: Iron Fist]]''</ref> and [[Iron Fist (Executor-class)|''Iron Fist'']].<ref name="X-Wing: Solo Command">''[[X-Wing: Solo Command]]''</ref> A wing of B-wings also served against [[Delak Krennel]] and his [[Ciutric Hegemony]].<ref name="X-Wing: Isard's Revenge">''[[X-Wing: Isard's Revenge]]''</ref> The New Republic's [[Green Squadron (New Republic)|Green Squadron]] was partially made up of B-wings at the time of the [[Battle of Calamari]],<ref name="CSWEGS">{{CSWECite|I|367|Green Squadron (3)}}</ref> and B-wing squadrons were present for [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Natasi Daala]]'s later [[Attack on Mon Calamari|attack]] on [[Dac/Legends|Mon Calamari]],<ref name="Dark" /> the [[Battle of Adumar]],<ref name="X-Wing: Starfighters of Adumar">''[[X-Wing: Starfighters of Adumar]]''</ref> and the [[Battle of Almania]].<ref name="The New Rebellion">''[[The New Rebellion]]''</ref> [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] flew a B-wing into [[Nam Chorios/Legends|Nam Chorios]].<ref name="Planet of Twilight">''[[Planet of Twilight]]''</ref>

As it was designed by Admiral Ackbar, Mon Calamari such as Ackbar and Terpfen used expanded versions as their personal shuttles, while other Mon Calamari pilots flew the starfighter into battle, such as [[Twin Suns Squadron]]'s [[Beelyath]] as part of the [[Battle of Borleias (Yuuzhan Vong War; Second)|Second Battle of Borleias]].<ref name="Enemy Lines I: Rebel Dream">''[[The New Jedi Order: Enemy Lines I: Rebel Dream]]''</ref><ref name="Enemy Lines II: Rebel Stand">''[[The New Jedi Order: Enemy Lines II: Rebel Stand]]''</ref> Another group besides the New Republic noted for its use of the B-wing was the Verpine, who preferred to use the craft in high-speed bombing runs if defending their territory was necessary.<ref name="The Courtship of Princess Leia">''[[The Courtship of Princess Leia]]''</ref>

[[File:B-wing_helmet.jpg|thumb|right|220px|A B-wing [[Pilot/Legends|pilot's]] helmet]]

Some B-wings would be modified to have a [[YT-series/Legends|YT-series]] cockpit and a [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolaser]] cannon, making them [[Ugly/Legends|uglies]]. These were called [[Corellian/B-wing Ugly|Corellian/B-wing uglies]].<ref name="Ambush at Corellia">''[[Ambush at Corellia]]''</ref> These modified B-wings were used by the [[Sacorrian Triad]] during the [[Corellian Crisis|First Corellian Insurrection]], but were largely unsuccessful against the Bakuran fleet that opposed them.<ref name="Showdown at Centerpoint">''[[Showdown at Centerpoint]]''</ref>

B-wings continued to play the vital role of [[Heavy assault starfighter/Legends|heavy assault starfighter]] for the New Republic and its successor, the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]], throughout the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] War in all major engagements, including the [[Battle of Coruscant (Yuuzhan Vong War)|Battle of Coruscant]]<ref name="Star by Star">''[[The New Jedi Order: Star by Star]]''</ref> and [[Battle of Yuuzhan'tar]],<ref name="The Unifying Force">''[[The New Jedi Order: The Unifying Force]]''</ref> the [[Battle of Ebaq]],<ref name="Destiny's Way">''[[The New Jedi Order: Destiny's Way]]''</ref> and the Second Battle of [[Borleias/Legends|Borleias]]. In a particular unique use during the latter instance, a Twin Suns pilot named Beelyath and his gunner, [[Sharr Latt]], launched the decoy [[Goddess missile]] from his B-wing, luring several [[Yorik-et|coralskippers]] to their doom.<ref name="Enemy Lines II: Rebel Stand" />

The B-wing fighter continued to serve in the Galactic Alliance Fleet through the [[Dark Nest Crisis]]/[[Swarm War]] and the [[Second Galactic Civil War]]. Over a century after it was introduced, the B-wing served as the inspiration for the [[Besh-type personal starfighter|''Besh''-type personal starfighter]].

==Behind the scenes==
The B-wing fighter was designed by [[Joe Johnston]] and [[Bill George]]. The craft derives its name from the fact that the crew labeled the two new Rebel starfighter models in ''Return of the Jedi'' as "A fighter" and "B fighter". While the [[A-wing]] looks similar to a capital A, the B-wing, on first glance, does not resemble its namesake. However, when viewed upon from a certain angle, it looks like a lowercase b. Bill George had so much input into the starship's development, that his colleagues nicknamed it the "Bill-Wing Fighter".<ref name="Sculpting">''[[Sculpting a Galaxy: Inside the Star Wars Model Shop]]''</ref>

''[[Star Wars: The Blueprints]]'' states that no B-wing cockpit set was ever built for filming pilot footage; however, it contains a drawing of a B-wing cockpit mislabelled as an A-wing cockpit, possibly indicating that the B-wing cockpit was indeed built and filmed for ''Return of the Jedi''.

[[File:MCQ-B-WingsAttackStarDestroyer.png|thumb|left|250px|B-wing concept production painting by [[Ralph McQuarrie]]]]
The craft's unusually thin shape was problematic for blue-screen photography; the model tended to blend into the starfield. As a consequence, some planned sequences with the B-wing were cut from the original release of [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']], and the B-wing is not explicitly shown in action during the Battle of Endor in the film. In fact, after the ships fly away from the still-active Death Star II shield at the start of the battle, the B-wing is hardly seen at all. The rotating cockpit design of the B-wing was based on early concept art for the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']].<ref name="DB" />

The appearance of the B-wing in the [[Star Wars: Droids: The Adventures of R2-D2 and C-3PO|''Star Wars Droids'']] episodes "[[The New King]]" and "[[Escape Into Terror]]" and intro of every episode is disputed,<ref name="LC">{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=152583&start=980#15895005|thread=Holocron continuity database questions|user=[[Leland Chee|Leland Y Chee]]|date=2006-11-06|time=6:03 PM|quote=Droids animated series B-wing: Likely, it's some sort of predecessor like the H-60 Tempest bomber.}}</ref> since canon states the B-wing was developed shortly before the Battle of Yavin and ''Droids'' is set in 15 BBY.

B-wings are made to land with the cockpit on the right side. However in ''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader]]'' and ''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]'' the B-Wing hovers in the hangar with the cockpit on the left side. Still in these two games, for technical reasons, it is impossible to make the cockpit spin as the ship rotates.

Many sources like ''[[Star Wars: Complete Cross-Sections]]'' and ''[[Star Wars: Battles for the Galaxy]]'' call the laser cannon a heavy one while not giving a grade to the ion cannons, suggesting them to be medium. ''[[Star Wars: Head-to-Head]]'' repeatedly calls the ion cannons heavy (with mentioning the heavy laser in the text but forgetting it in the stats). In contrast, ''[[Starships of the Galaxy]]'', its [[Starships of the Galaxy (Saga Edition)|Saga Edition]] and the [[Star Wars: Age of Rebellion Core Rulebook|''Star Wars: Age of Rebellion'' Core Rulebook]] call the ion cannons light ones because their role-playing game mechanics restrict stronger weapons to larger craft.

In 2000, LEGO released a set titled "B-wing at Rebel Control Center" which included a B-wing and a rebel command center with B-wing pilot, Rebel mechanic, and R5-D4 minifigures. LEGO released another set in 2006 titled "B-wing Fighter", which included an improved model, a display stand, and two minifigures: Ten Numb and a Rebel pilot. In 2012, LEGO released an Ultimate Collector Series edition of the B-wing that included a bigger, non-minifigure display model of the ship, a stand with name plaque and no minifigures. In 2014, another minifigure scaled B-wing (#75050) was released with three minifigures: Ten Numb, General Airen Cracken and a Gray Squadron Pilot.
